definition: A Rust Event realization constructs owned immutable occurrence data. It does not publish, persist, register, deduplicate or claim delivery of the event.
shape: Separate private-field occurrence, payload and event structs retain occurrence identity, event type, version and occurred-at identity. Public owned input carriers are consumed by one fallible constructor.

values.decimal: finite f64 with negative zero normalized

time: Required time is explicit input. Generated time requires an explicit borrowed synchronous clock, called exactly once after all input validation; ambient clocks are forbidden.
ownership: Construction moves validated input fields into the result. Getters borrow; no mutable field or setter is exported.
module: One collision-free module per qualified selector under src/domain/events. Reference carriers are local semantic identities, not embedded target objects.
verification: Deterministic planning, Cargo construction for required and generated time, one-call clock evidence, validation failures and private-field compile-fail controls are required.
compatibility: Existing source schema and generators remain unchanged. This candidate is selected only by reconciled Rust and has no default cutover.
